name: Cutter Shorts (Denim Cut-Off, Hemmed by Hand)
description: Jeans that lost their lower half — to damage, to heat, or to deliberate cutting — and were hemmed with whatever thread was available. The hem line is rarely straight. Sometimes the raw edge is left intentionally, fraying into a soft border. A the Gray Zone summer staple because they cost nothing extra if you already have ruined jeans. Worn with leggings in winter.
what_it_says: You waste nothing. When something breaks, you find the next use for it.
story_hooks: The lower half of these jeans still exists — someone else is wearing the legs as makeshift sleeves.
A specific pair's denim is cut from jeans that were worn during a notable the Gray Zone incident; someone recognizes the fabric pattern.

physical_description.visual_profile: Truncated denim silhouette ending mid-thigh, deliberately casual and utilitarian. The uneven hemline creates an asymmetrical, hand-finished look that reads as street-authentic rather than styled. Conveys resourcefulness and thermal practicality.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the hip and thigh, following the original jeans' cut. No tapering at the leg opening due to the abrupt hem.
physical_description.primary_material: Indigo or faded denim, often salvaged from damaged or discarded jeans. Weave shows signs of wear.
physical_description.texture: Stiff in the body with visible stitching irregularities. Hem edge is deliberately rough or unevenly frayed; raw threads fray outward creating a soft, feathered border.
physical_description.color_scheme: Faded indigo base with darker inseam and waistband. Accent thread color varies—copper, white, black, or mismatched tones depending on what was available.
physical_description.closures: Original jean zipper and button fly, fully functional.
distinctive_features: Raw denim edge left intentionally fraying
Fading patterns from previous wear and sun exposure
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4-5 functional/salvage. Zero cost, zero pretense.
physical_description.cultural_context: the Gray Zone, ungoverned zones, summer survival. Worn by those who cannot afford new clothing and refuse to waste damaged jeans. Signals resilience, resourcefulness, and rejection of corpo fashion cycles.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn-in, sun-faded, thread loose at hem edges, small tears or stains from daily use. Looks better the more lived-in it becomes.
